question: How does the Catholic doctrine of the resurrection of the body differ from Platonic immortality of the soul?

choices.A: Plato taught the body is a prison the immortal soul escapes at death; Catholic teaching holds the body is good and will be raised and glorified — the whole person, body and soul, is destined for eternal life
choices.B: Catholic teaching agrees with Plato that the body is irrelevant to final salvation
choices.C: Catholic theology denies any form of soul survival after death until the resurrection
choices.D: The resurrection and Platonic immortality are identical concepts in different vocabularies

teaching.title: Resurrection vs. Platonic Immortality
teaching.body: Platonism views the body as a tomb (soma-sema) that imprisons the divine soul; death liberates the soul into pure incorporeal existence. Biblical Christianity (Jewish and Christian) teaches the opposite: the body is God's good creation, and the goal is not escape from the body but resurrection of the body — 'the resurrection of the dead' in the Creed. Paul in 1 Corinthians 15 extensively argues for bodily resurrection using seed and harvest imagery. The risen Christ still had a body, though glorified. This is why care for the dying and burial of the dead are sacred acts in Catholic tradition.
